The Recursive Agents Hackathon
San Francisco, CASat, Oct 17 at 9:00 AM – 10:00 PM (PDT)

Build a team of agents you can walk away from.

During the PyTorch Conference in San Francisco, build agents that can take a goal and run with it. Let them make the plan, spin up sub-agents, delegate work, communicate with each other, check their own progress, recover when things break, and keep going.

Get a head start. Crusoe is hosting Field Day the day before the hackathon. You'll join a random team and race to take a model from raw data to production. Friday, Oct 16, 1-5pm. Spots are limited, register here!

Push beyond the one-shot agent into persistent loops that rarely need you involved: agents building teams and handling delegation, memory, and long-running inference that can keep operating after you walk away until the work is complete

Build on Crusoe Managed Inference and put leading open models, including NVIDIA’s Nemotron family, into production on high-performance NVIDIA infrastructure.

Compete to win $25,000 in cash prizes and an NVIDIA RTX 5090.

Note: This event is fully in-person in San Francisco. Teams may have up to four members. All attendees must apply and be approved to attend.

Register

Approved participants will compete for $25,000 in cash prizes and an NVIDIA RTX 5090.

candidates.title: Multiplayer Hackathon by Party - #SFTechWeek
candidates.evidence:
Multiplayer Hackathon by Party - #SFTechWeek
Multiplayer Building is here.

Google Docs made documents collaborative. Figma made design collaborative. Now, Party is making building collaborative.

Most hackathons are a room full of people, each one alone with their own agent. This one works the other way around.

At this event, you'll spend a full day building with agent teams: together, in the open. We pack the room with founders, engineers, product leaders, hackers, and designers, split into teams, and everyone steers the agents together. Agent teams do the heavy lifting on objectives (not prompts) while your whole team directs them in the same live session. Every contribution has a name on it.

You'll leave with something you helped build (hosted publicly), some new friends, and a totally refreshed outlook on building great products.

This event is absolutely free. We're putting up $25,000 in token credits as prizes. You'll join the rest of the group on our community Party space where the tokens are free and you can see and steer everything that's cooking.

What you'll do:

-We'll add you to the community Party space
-Form a team, or join one when you arrive
-Build, review, and ship a real project alongside your team and its agents
-Demo what you made to the room
-Enjoy food, refreshments, and a day with other passionate builders

What to Expect:

9:30 – 10:00 AM | Doors, Breakfast & Team Formation Grab coffee and breakfast, get your laptop set up, find your team.

10:00 – 10:30 AM | Welcome & Walkthrough What we're building toward, how Party works, the tracks, and how judging works.

10:30 AM | Hacking Begins

12:30 PM | Lunch - brought in, keep building or take a break

4:30 PM | Code Freeze

4:45 – 5:45 PM | Demos & Judging Every team demos. Judges score live.

5:45 – 6:00 PM | Awards

Prizes:

$25,000 in token credits, awarded across:

-Grand Prize / Best Built Together: $10,000
-Best Use of Multiple Agents: $5,000
-Most Shippable: $5,000
-People's Choice: $5,000

Judged by the Party team and our sponsors.

Who Should Attend:

-AI-pilled engineers curious what building in the open feels like

-Product managers and designers who want to be more involved in the build

-Founders and early startup teams looking to ship faster with better quality

-Project managers and technical leads

-Anyone on the Peninsula who'd like to spend a Saturday building with like-minded individuals

You do not need to be an expert with coding agents. You do not need to arrive with a team - we'll help you find one. You do need to be up for building something with people you've just met.

What You'll Walk Away With:

-Something real that you helped build - that you'll have access to after the event

-The experience of building alongside others, with agents, to create something spectacular

-A shot at $25,000 in token credits

-Three months of Party Starter, free - which includes $20 in credits, monthly

-$250 in credits so you can keep building

Important Details:

-Format: In person, full day

-What to bring: Your laptop. Breakfast, lunch, and snacks are on us.

-Experience level: All levels. Party, Cursor, Claude Code, etc. experience not required.

-Teams: Teams of 2-5. Come with one or form one at the event.

-Capacity: Limited to 100. RSVP required

-Location: Downtown Redwood City, Peninsula

Event Info

🎟 Registration: RSVP required 

🍽 Food & Drinks: Breakfast, lunch, snacks, and drinks provided

🏢 Venue: 810 Hamilton - our event space in downtown Redwood City

📍 Address: 810 Hamilton St, Redwood City, CA 94063

🚗 Parking: Street parking on the surrounding blocks & parking structure on Jefferson St.

🚉 Transit: One block from the Redwood City Caltrain station. Approximately 25 min Caltrain ride from 4th & King.

About Party

Party is the multiplayer workspace where your whole team builds together alongside fleets of agents, out in the open. Agent Flows do the heavy lifting while humans steer. You pick the harness and model for each agent in the Flow — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Opencode — and work in the same secure session as the rest of your team. Bring your own keys, or use ours.

Learn more about Party at party.build. Try Party at app.party.build (web, MacOS, iOS, and Android).

This event is a part of #SFTechWeek—a week of events hosted by VCs and startups to bring together the tech ecosystem. Learn more at www.tech-week.com

HostsSnowflake & Anthropic
Intelligence at Work Hackathon
Menlo Park, CAFri, Oct 23 at 8:30 AM – 8:00 PM (PDT)

Bring a real problem from your company. Build a solution with Claude and Snowflake.

Join Snowflake and Anthropic at the Silicon Valley AI Hub for Intelligence at Work, a day of hands-on building alongside engineers, product builders, and data teams.

Build something that makes the business run better, from getting people from question to decision faster to automating recurring multi-step work, or change what the business offers by creating a new product or reimagining a customer experience, all grounded in what your company actually knows.

Bring your own data and put it to work. Company data approved for use is preferred, and relevant public data is welcome. A fallback dataset will be available if needed.

Prizes, speakers, and judges to be announced soon. Stay tuned.

Note: This event is fully in person in Menlo Park. Space is limited. Teams may have up to three members. All attendees must apply and be approved, then confirm their attendance.

#SFTechWeek - Decision-Grade AI @ Stanford ⚡️ A Buildathon on LLM Trust
Saturday, Oct 10
10:30am – 4:00pm
PTET
Remind me
Hosted by Ezio, TokenRouter
AA
+8
1881 Page Mill Rd - Industrious Palo Alto Page Mill
AI is becoming powerful enough to act. Now it needs to become trustworthy enough to deserve that power. Let’s create a sandbox for AI Trust together. As LLMs and AI agents move from generating text to influencing real decisions, the cost of confident mistakes gets much higher. A polished answer isn’t enough. We need systems that can verify claims, evaluate evidence, surface uncertainty, detect fragile reasoning, and decide when an output is trustworthy enough to act on. Decision-Grade AI is a Stanford-based panel discussion + buildathon bringing together technical builders to prototype that missing layer. Over the course of the event, we will have an exclusive panel discussion and buildathon. ☕ Food & Drinks: We've got you covered with coffee, water, refreshing drinks, a delicious lunch, and snacks throughout the event.Opening Talk: Kiana Jafari, Executive Director @ Stanford Center for AI Safety Featured Panelists: Bryant McCombs, GTM @ OpenAI Clark Barrett, Computer Scientist @ Stanford Wesley Deng, Senior Researcher @ Microsoft Sarath Swaminathan, Research Scientist @ IBM What You’ll Build: AI is getting better at producing answers. We want to build the systems that determine whether those answers deserve to drive decisions. SCHEDULE: 10:30–11:00 AM | Check-in, coffee & team mixing 11:00 AM–11:40 AM | Technical kickoff & demos 11:40 AM - 12:00 PM | Opening Talk - Kiana Jafari 12:00–1:00 PM | Expert Panel Discussion (Lunch Afterwards) 1:00–1:15 PM | Challenge reveal & team formation 1:15–3:00 PM | Build with mentor support 3:00–4:00 PM | Final demos, judging & awards **Snacks throughoutTeams will tackle one of three core challenges -→ Approval Gate→ Before You Act→ Build Trust AgentWe’ll start with a technical kickoff introducing the problem space, example architectures, tools, and build directions. After the expert panel, teams will choose a challenge and build with mentor support before presenting working prototypes in final demos. This is not a hackathon about building another chatbot. It’s about building the infrastructure underneath the next generation of AI systems - the tools that help answer: Can we verify this? What evidence supports it? How confident should we be? Should a human or agent actually act on it? Our team has been exploring these questions through Ezio, where we’re developing approaches to evaluating AI outputs in real time. This buildathon opens the challenge up to a broader community of builders interested in making AI systems more reliable, auditable, and decision-ready. Who should attend: CS, engineering, and data science students; AI/ML researchers; software engineers; technical founders; product builders; recent technical alumni; and designers interested in LLM evaluation, verification, model robustness, or agent reliability. You don’t need prior experience in AI safety. You just need to want to build systems that make AI harder to fool - and safer to trust. Exceptional builders. One day. Build the trust layer for AI. Cohost 1 - TokenRouter Verified Models with Enterprise-grade Controls. TokenRouter helps companies use the world's leading AI models with the security and control their business requires. It brings more than 140 verified models together in one place so teams can build faster and scale with confidence. Cohost 2 - Ezio Ezio is the trust layer for AI agents and LLM outputs, measuring AI-generated responses before they are used in high-stakes workflows.This event is a part of #SFTechWeek—a week of events hosted by VCs and startups to bring together the tech ecosystem. Learn more at www.tech-week.com Cohost 3: HarnessRouter HarnessRouter brings 20 of the world’s leading agent harnesses into your product as runtime infrastructure. By combining agent harnesses with models, skills, and tools, builders can create agents for contract review and redlining, academic research, video editing, and more. Every task runs in an isolated sandbox, with managed concurrency and a consistent interface for tasks, sessions, files, artifacts, and traces, helping teams move from prototype to production without operating the underlying agent infrastructure.
